newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's big Chelyabinsk alloy plant boosts output.
newsitem.headline: Russia's big Chelyabinsk alloy plant boosts output.

text.p: Russia's giant Chelyabinsk electro-metallurgical combine produced 172,000 tonnes of ferro-alloys in the first five months, a 57.6 percent rise on year-ago levels, Prime-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.

Output at the Urals plant, known as CHEMK, included 82,000 tonnes of ferro-silicone (6.5 percent more than year-ago levels), 55,000 tonnes of ferro-chrome (a 267 percent rise), 29,500 tonnes of silicone chrome (a 265 percent increase) and 15,500 tonnes of electrodes (a 36.5 percent boost).
Tass quoted a plant official as saying the rise was due to steady chrome ore supplies from Kazakhstan and Turkey and to development of the plant's captive ore supply.

Tass put total ferro-alloys output at the plant in 1996 at 309,000 tonnes, a drop of 16 percent on 1995's level. Production included 55,000 tonnes of ferro-chrome, 199,000 tonnes of ferro-silicone, 60,000 tonnes of silicone manganese and 28,000 tonnes of electrodes, it said.
CHEMK, with 29 operational furnaces, is one of the biggest alloys plants in the world and Russia's top alloys producer.
It supplies, among others, Glencore AG of Switzerland and British firm RCS. The latter and private Antwerp-based B and D Industrial Group BV are among those with stakes in the plant.
